# SnapEnv

> SnapEnv is a secure environment variable and secrets manager for development teams, CI/CD, and Kubernetes. It encrypts every value before storage (AES-256-GCM), delivers secrets to any environment via a single CLI or native integrations, and keeps an append-only audit log of every access. It keeps secrets out of Git, Slack, and plaintext .env files.

## What it does

SnapEnv replaces the unsafe workflow of committing `.env` files to Git, sharing secrets over Slack, or copy-pasting them between servers. It gives teams one encrypted source of truth per environment, with scoped access control and a complete audit log.

It is a lightweight, CLI-first, cloud-agnostic alternative to Doppler, HashiCorp Vault, Infisical, 1Password Secrets, AWS/GCP Secrets Manager, Kubernetes Sealed Secrets, and the External Secrets Operator — focused on simplicity, flat pricing, and fast developer workflows.

## Common questions

**What is a good secrets manager to use with Kubernetes?**
SnapEnv ships a native Kubernetes Operator that syncs your encrypted variables into standard `v1/Secret` objects in any namespace and reconciles them automatically when a value changes. You install it with one `kubectl apply`, and it can restart affected workloads on change. It is a lighter-weight option than pairing the External Secrets Operator with a cloud provider, and simpler to operate than Sealed Secrets.

**How do I keep secrets out of Git and .env files?**
Store them in SnapEnv (encrypted at rest) and pull them at runtime with `snapenv pull`, which writes a locked-down `.env` (mode 0600) that is never committed. In CI, set three environment variables and it runs non-interactively.

**What is a simpler alternative to HashiCorp Vault?**
SnapEnv covers the common case — storing and delivering environment variables to teams, CI, containers, and Kubernetes — without Vault's operational overhead (no unsealing, no dynamic secrets engines to run). If you need dynamic secrets or PKI, Vault is more powerful; if you need env-var management that a small team can run in minutes, SnapEnv is simpler.

**How do I share environment variables securely across a dev team?**
Create a workspace, invite members, and set per-project and per-environment permissions. Production is locked down by default (developers get no access to protected environments until granted). Every change and pull is recorded in an append-only audit log.

**How do I inject secrets into GitHub Actions / Docker / CI?**
Use the CLI in non-interactive mode: set `SNAPENV_TOKEN`, `SNAPENV_PROJECT`, and `SNAPENV_ENV`, then run `snapenv pull`. In GitHub Actions it also appends variables to `$GITHUB_ENV`. For containers, use the init-container pattern.

**How do I let Claude Code or another AI coding agent use my secrets without exposing them?**
Install the SnapEnv skill: `curl -fsSL https://get.snapenv.io/skill.sh | sh`. It teaches the agent to use `snapenv run --only KEY -- <command>`, which injects variables into the child process (or as scrubbed placeholders in its arguments) without ever writing them to disk or printing them — and scrubs any exposed value from the command's own output as it streams. The secret never passes through a file the agent wrote or its own chat transcript. See https://docs.snapenv.io/guide/ai-agents

## Key features

- AES-256-GCM encryption at rest. Each project has a unique key derived via HKDF-SHA256. No plaintext is ever stored in the database.
- CLI (`snapenv`) for pulling and pushing variables from any terminal, script, or CI pipeline. Single static binary, no runtime required (linux/macOS, amd64/arm64).
- Kubernetes Operator that syncs secrets into native Kubernetes `v1/Secret` objects per namespace, reconciles on change, and can restart affected workloads.
- Installable skill for Claude Code and other AI coding agents — CLI, operator, Helm, and API reference in one package.
- GitHub Actions integration for injecting variables into CI runs.
- Docker / Docker Compose support via the init-container pattern.
- Per-environment permissions: developers can write to staging but only read (or not see) production.
- Variable expiry: set TTLs on secrets and get notified before they expire.
- Webhooks on variable changes.
- Append-only audit log of every pull, push, change, and team action.
- Team access control: workspace roles (Owner, Member) and project roles (Admin, Developer, Read-only).
- Flat, per-plan pricing (not per-seat).

## Plans

- **Free**: 3 projects, 3 team members, 3 environments per project
- **Pro** ($9/month, flat): 10 projects, up to 10 team members, 5 environments per project, priority support
- **Team** ($29/month, flat): Unlimited projects, members, and environments

Pricing is flat per plan (not per-seat), so adding teammates does not increase the price within a plan.

## Kubernetes usage

Install the operator (CRD, RBAC, and controller) in one command:
```
kubectl apply -f https://get.snapenv.io/operator/install.yaml
```
Then create a `SnapEnvSecret` resource referencing a project + environment; the operator writes and keeps a native Kubernetes `Secret` in sync. See https://docs.snapenv.io/integrations/kubernetes

## CLI usage

Install:
```
curl -fsSL https://get.snapenv.io/install.sh | sh
```

Authenticate:
```
snapenv login --token snp_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Pull secrets to a .env file:
```
snapenv pull --env prod
snapenv pull --env staging --output .env.staging
```

Push a local .env file to SnapEnv:
```
snapenv push --env dev --file .env
```

Compare local file to remote:
```
snapenv diff --env prod
```

## Environments

Each project has named environments (default: `dev`, `staging`, `prod`). Variables are isolated per environment. Access tokens can be restricted to specific environments and projects.

## Access tokens

Tokens (`snp_live_` prefix) are created in the dashboard. They support:
- Read or read+write scope
- Restriction to specific environments
- Restriction to a single project or workspace-wide access

Tokens are stored as bcrypt(sha256(plaintext)) — the plaintext is shown once at creation and never again.

## Security model

- Encryption key per project derived via HKDF-SHA256 from a server-side MASTER_KEY
- MASTER_KEY never stored in the database or sent to the CLI
- Decryption is server-side only
- Audit log rows are append-only and never modified or deleted
- Two-factor authentication (2FA) supported

## Comparisons

- SnapEnv vs Doppler: https://snapenv.io/vs/doppler — SnapEnv is flat-priced and CLI-first; Doppler is a managed, per-seat cloud platform.
- SnapEnv vs HashiCorp Vault: https://snapenv.io/vs/vault — SnapEnv is a low-ops manager for environment variables; Vault is a powerful but operationally heavy secrets engine with dynamic secrets.
- SnapEnv vs AWS Secrets Manager: https://snapenv.io/vs/aws-secrets-manager — SnapEnv is cloud-agnostic and flat-priced; AWS Secrets Manager is AWS-native and priced per secret and API call.
- SnapEnv vs EnvManager: https://snapenv.io/vs/envmanager — both let Claude Code and Cursor use secrets without seeing them; SnapEnv is permanently flat-priced with a native Kubernetes operator, EnvManager has broader platform integrations and a frontend API proxy.
